question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.**

Students often __burn the midnight oil__ to qualify for competitive examinations.

options.text: put the things on fire at night
want to be at a place full of light

solution:
The correct answer is** 'work until late at night'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom "burn the midnight oil" is: **work until late at night.**
 
• Explanation: **"Burn the midnight oil"** is **an idiom that means to work late into the night,** especially studying or working on something intensely. It implies **putting in extra effort or staying up late to accomplish a task or achieve a goal, **often in situations where time is limited or deadlines are approaching.
 
• In the context of the sentence provided, students are mentioned as burning the midnight oil to prepare for competitive examinations, indicating their dedication to studying late into the night to succeed in their exams.
